title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: Chicken braised in red wine
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces slow-cooked in red wine with smoked bacon, mushrooms, and pearl onions. A French bistro classic that is ideal for cooking ahead.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin is one of the most recognised dishes of French country cooking. The dish as it is now known was codified in the twentieth century, though chicken cooked in wine appears in French regional cooking much earlier.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy pot that can go from hob to oven.

content.text: Coq au vin is bone-in chicken pieces braised in red wine with smoked bacon, mushrooms, and pearl onions. The chicken cooks slowly in the wine, the sauce reduces to something rich and dark, and the whole thing improves if you leave it a day and reheat it. Serve with buttered egg noodles or creamy mash.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides in batches, about 4 minutes per batch. Lift out and set aside. Add the bacon lardons to the pot and cook for 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the butter, onion, and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the flour and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the red wine and stock. Scrape the base of the pot. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Return the chicken, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over a low heat for 45 minutes.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms to the pot. Cook uncovered for a further 20 minutes until the sauce has reduced slightly and the vegetables are tender.
Remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves. Taste for seasoning, scatter over the parsley, and serve.
